scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: I would say 0, you're not the ass in this situation. Here's why: 1. **You were genuine**: You didn't fake an emotional response just to meet your wife's expectations. You reacted naturally, focusing on your love for her rather than the dress. 2. **You didn't promise a specific reaction**: Your wife and her friend may have assumed you'd be overwhelmed with emotion, but you never explicitly promised to cry or have a certain reaction. 3. **The maid of honor's behavior was unfair**: It's understandable that you felt uncomfortable with her nudging you and trying to elicit a specific response. That could be seen as pressure or manipulation. 4. **You communicated your feelings**: After the fact, you explained your perspective to your wife, reassuring her that you were ecstatic to marry her, even if you didn't show it in the way she expected. 5. **You didn't intend to hurt your wife's feelings**: It's clear that you care about your wife's feelings, but you also can't force yourself to have a certain emotional response. It's possible that your wife was caught up in the romantic ideal of a fairytale wedding, and your reaction didn't fit that narrative. However, it's essential to remember that every person is unique, and emotional responses can vary greatly. Perhaps have an open and empathetic conversation with your wife to understand her perspective and feelings. You might say something like, "I understand that you had a certain vision for our wedding, and I'm sorry if my reaction didn't meet your expectations. However, I want you to know that my love and commitment to you are genuine, even if I didn't show it in the way you hoped."
